w:r.w:t: IOGP Report 510 — Operating Management System Framework
The current approved revision is maintained in the ACME document repository. Printed copies are uncontrolled unless separately registered.

“Shall” and “must” establish mandatory ACME obligations. “Should” identifies a recommended practice; “may” identifies an allowed option. Any permitted departure from a mandatory requirement follows the authorised deviation process.

OMS tags placed below a document title or heading identify the OMS expectations addressed by that document or section. A tag listed on a parent heading is not automatically a direct tag on its subsections.

This procedure establishes a consistent method for recognising, assessing, authorising, implementing and closing changes that may affect ACME Energy Limited’s operational risks or performance. It is intended to prevent unintended consequences when the basis of a design, operating activity, organisation, procedure or safeguard is altered.

Management of Change (MOC) is a risk-based process. The required review effort varies with the significance of the proposed change, but documentation, accountability and approval requirements remain in place for every change determined to be within scope.

The procedure applies to ACME-controlled facilities, associated projects and operating functions, and to contractors proposing or implementing changes under ACME operational control. It includes permanent, temporary and urgent changes that can affect equipment, materials, systems, operating conditions, personnel capability, procedures or important business interfaces.

Replacement in kind within the approved specification, configuration and operating limits may be managed through established maintenance processes. A replacement shall not be considered in kind solely because a component has a similar name or nominal capacity. Any uncertainty about technical equivalence is referred to the Technical Authority.
Changes affecting a safety-critical function, a technical operating limit or an established risk-control basis shall be screened under MOC before implementation.
A proposed departure from an approved baseline in plant, people, activity, method or document.
Role accountable for coordinating the MOC from initiation through closure.
Designated reviewer of technical adequacy and relevant engineering standards.
Operational authority for readiness and safe execution in the affected area.
Designated role with delegated authority for the MOC decision.
Change approved for a defined duration and subject to restoration or renewal.

The normal sequence is: identify and register the change; confirm its classification; determine the review scope; assess risk and technical implications; define actions and approvals; verify readiness; implement under work controls; and close the record after evidence of completion has been accepted.
The granting of MOC approval is not a permit to work and does not authorise personnel to bypass isolation, permit, handover or operational control requirements.

The proposer shall describe the intended outcome and the existing approved baseline. Reviewers shall consider interfaces outside the immediate work scope. Approval shall be granted by a role independent of initiation when the delegated-approval framework requires such separation. Conditions attached to an approval shall be carried into the implementation plan.
Defines the need, scope, baseline and proposed outcome.
Coordinates screening, review, actions, implementation and closure.
Confirms operational readiness and interfaces with work control.
Reviews engineering implications, standards and safeguards.
Reviews hazards, environmental and personnel-risk implications.
Approves, rejects or returns the MOC within delegated authority.
Controls record completeness and document revision / publication.
The Change Owner shall maintain the change record, identify affected functions, coordinate reviewers and ensure approval conditions are not lost during implementation.

The Technical Authority shall identify applicable standards, operating boundaries and equipment integrity implications. The HSE Adviser shall advise on the sufficiency of risk assessment and applicable risk controls.
The Area Authority shall verify that operations are prepared for the change and that the permitted work and handover arrangements reflect the approved change conditions.
R = performs; A = accountable; C = consulted; I = informed. HSE Adviser participates according to risk-screening results; Document Controller manages controlled-record and publishing activities.
Change Initiator records the proposed change, affected asset or process, requested timing and reason for change.
Change Owner identifies the existing design, operational or organisational baseline and describes what will differ.
Change Owner records the affected functions, facilities, documents and known interfaces.
Technical Authority or suitable delegate confirms whether technical equivalence is demonstrated where replacement in kind is proposed.

The initial screen considers potential changes to process conditions, equipment integrity, controls, safeguarding systems, competence, work instructions, legal conditions, external commitments and simultaneous operations. The record identifies whether a temporary, permanent or urgent process applies.

A minor modification at equipment level may affect a common utility, interlock or operating interface. The screen shall consider system-wide consequences rather than the apparent scale of the physical modification.
Change Owner proposes the scope and depth of assessment based on consequences and uncertainty.
Technical Authority identifies required discipline reviews, verification or calculations.
HSE Adviser confirms whether additional risk methods or regulatory consultation are required.
Change Owner records review assignments, open questions and target completion dates.

The review team shall examine what the change is intended to achieve, how it changes the existing risk profile, which safeguards may be affected, how operations and maintenance will respond, and how the change will be verified before use. Documentation reviewed may include drawings, design records, operating limits, incident experience and maintenance histories.
Changes affecting significant risk controls shall identify the existing and proposed control function, performance expectation, verification method and accountable owner before the approval decision.

The Technical Authority determines which technical disciplines must participate. Reviewers consider the suitability of materials, design margins, equipment and instrument specifications, interfaces, maintainability, reliability, operating envelope and impacts on safeguards. The need for independent verification is determined by the technical risk and delegated engineering rules.
The Technical Authority shall confirm the sufficiency of the technical review and document all outstanding conditions before the proposal is submitted to the Approving Authority.
Review is complete; action list and residual-risk basis documented.
Missing information, verification or risk controls identified.
Proposal inconsistent with required controls, standards or acceptable risk.
Conditions assigned, tracked and verified before affected work or service.

The Approving Authority reviews the proposed change, technical and risk assessments, consultation, open actions, required resources and readiness arrangements. An approval may be conditional. The decision record shall identify the approver, decision date, scope and restrictions.
The Approving Authority shall not release a change for implementation while unresolved actions invalidate the basis on which the risk was assessed.

The Change Owner establishes an implementation plan that defines sequencing, field activities, required operating procedures, competencies, materials, work controls, inspections, contingency arrangements and handover points. It records who confirms readiness and when work may proceed.
The implementation plan shall list required drawings, instructions, training, equipment records and work-control documents to be updated before or after start-up, with dates and accountable roles.
Area Authority checks that required permits, isolations, interfaces and shift arrangements are ready for the approved work.
Technical Authority verifies required design and safeguarding checks have been completed.
Change Owner confirms training, documentation, communications and outstanding action conditions.
Area Authority records readiness and formally releases the work under applicable operating controls.
Where a critical safeguard is impaired or an unplanned condition emerges, the work shall be stopped and reassessed under the approved operating and MOC controls.

Personnel shall execute only the reviewed and approved scope. A deviation that changes technical intent, risk controls, configuration or operating assumptions requires evaluation and, where material, renewed MOC review and approval. Verbal agreement does not replace the controlled decision record.

The Area Authority accepts the updated equipment or activity after required tests, verifications and conditions have been completed. The handover identifies current operating limits, temporary arrangements, open actions, monitoring needs and the responsible operational personnel.
Change Owner obtains evidence that work and verification are complete and identifies residual actions.
Technical Authority confirms that required design records and technical documents are current.
Area Authority confirms acceptance of the change in the operating configuration and handover record.
Document Controller verifies that approved document revisions are published and prior versions remain traceable.
Change Owner records the close-out decision and reports overdue significant actions for escalation.
The MOC record shall retain the proposal, baseline, screening, risk and technical reviews, approvals, implementation actions, readiness checks, deviations, handover and closure evidence.
Revised procedures and drawings are subject to their normal document-control and technical approval processes. MOC approval does not replace approval of an updated controlled procedure.

Temporary changes must have a clearly stated operational purpose, an expiry date, monitoring arrangements and a restoration or permanent-resolution plan. The Change Owner is responsible for advance review of approaching expiry and for verifying that temporary arrangements do not become indefinite by default.
Extension of a temporary change requires a documented reassessment and approval before expiry, using the delegated authority applicable to the revised risk.

An urgent operating need may require an expedited sequence of reviews, but the essential requirements for identifying hazards, consulting competent authorities, documenting decisions and verifying readiness remain. Emergency response actions under established emergency plans are distinct from changes to an approved operational baseline.
Where time does not permit the required review or competent authorisation, personnel shall maintain or place the operation in a safe condition rather than implement an uncontrolled change.

The Approving Authority and Change Owner shall support regular review of outstanding MOCs, overdue actions, temporary changes, recurrence of unplanned deviations and evidence of document closure. Findings shall feed process improvement, competency development and revision of the MOC procedure.
Approved record linked to actual revised configuration.
Named owner, completion date and verification evidence.
Expiry tracking and timely authorisation of extension or restoration.
Records of verifications and formal operational handover.

IOGP Report 510 (2014), Operating Management System Framework; ACME-OMS-POL-001, Operational Risk Management Policy; current ACME permit-to-work, operating-readiness, technical-authority and document-control procedures.
Supporting forms and registers are maintained by the Document Controller as controlled repository records. Their current revisions shall be used whenever an MOC is initiated or progressed.

The screening guide supports consistent recognition of changes, including changes that may not initially be described as engineering modifications. It shall be applied with judgement and shall not substitute for competent review of risks or technical requirements.
Does the proposal alter a design or equipment specification?
Technical standards, pressure containment, materials and integrity.
Does it affect the operating envelope?
Limits, alarms, interlocks, trips and operating instructions.
Does it change a barrier or safeguarding function?
Does it alter materials or process chemistry?
Compatibility, hazards, corrosion and environmental impacts.
Does it affect inspection or maintenance?
Access, intervals, competence and equipment reliability.
Does it create a new interface or simultaneous operation?
Does it change organisation or staffing?
Does it affect contractors or supply arrangements?
Specifications, controls, handover and supplier interfaces.
Does it require document or drawing changes?
Controlled revision, training and accessibility at point of use.
Does it establish a temporary operating arrangement?
Expiry, monitoring, restoration and extension authority.
Appendix B Approval and readiness evidence

The Change Owner coordinates the evidence set appropriate to the change. The listed items are checked as applicable and cross-referenced in the MOC record; an item marked not applicable shall retain a reason where its omission could affect a significant risk-control decision.
Approved equipment, system or organisational baseline identified.
Hazards, consequences and risk controls evaluated.
Technical Authority acceptance and conditions recorded.
Area Authority interfaces and readiness addressed.
Approving Authority decision and restrictions preserved.
Permits, isolation, communications and method confirmed.
Updated drawings, procedures and records published.
Area Authority accepts configuration and residual conditions.
Actions complete or specifically controlled and assigned.
Appendix C Change register and review

The MOC register provides a live view of the status of changes. It should allow responsible managers to distinguish items waiting for technical review, awaiting approval, approved but not implemented, implemented but not closed, and temporary changes approaching expiry. Management review shall focus on the risks associated with stalled activities, not solely the number of open records.
The Document Controller shall retain a traceable reference from the change register to each approval, technical record and final close-out disposition.

The Approving Authority reviews the ageing of changes, repeated exceptions, overdue temporary arrangements and instances where the procedure has not prevented unplanned change. The resulting improvement actions are assigned to named roles with completion evidence. Findings may lead to revisions of requirements, controls, training or organisational interfaces.
